name: Lake Tohopekaliga (Toho)
type: Shallow grass lake: offshore hydrilla, shell bars, reeds, pads and mats
pool: Regulated by the water management district;Drawn down every few years for habitat work
notes: Spawn under way. Protected flats and offshore hydrilla both hold big fish.
Peak of the trophy season. Fish the moons and the calm days.
Late spawners and the first post-spawn fish.
Post-spawn on grass lines and deeper hydrilla edges.
Shad spawn at dawn; bluegill bed on the full moon.
Summer pattern: hydrilla lines at 8 to 10 ft and the mats.
Hottest stretch. Fish first light, last light and after storms.
Hottest water. Current at the lock and canals helps.
Shad move into creeks and shoreline grass.
Fall feed. Bass follow shad into open pockets.
Cooler weather starts the speck bite.
Pre-spawn on offshore hydrilla; the first beds on warm spells.

flbass.doing: Cold fronts push bass to the outside grass lines and the deepest holes. Between fronts they slide toward the spawning flats, and the biggest fish of the year start to move.
how: Lipless crankbait or jerkbait over sparse hydrilla and eelgrass; slow it down after a front.
Punch mats with a 1 to 1.5 oz tungsten weight, or a slow Texas rig on the first hard edge.
Wild shiner under a float beside reed clumps and on outside grass: the trophy season.

specks.doing: Specks school in open water over the deepest flats, channels and offshore grass, suspended at a different depth from day to day.
how: Missouri minnows or grass shrimp, or spider-rig small jigs (hair jigs, tubes, Hal Flies).
Set minnows at several depths, then match the one that bites.
Cast a small jig to schools you see on forward-facing sonar.

bream.doing: Slow. Bluegill and shellcracker hold in deeper grass, canals and around docks; warm, sunny afternoons bring them up.
how: Grass shrimp on the bottom next to hydrilla or eelgrass.
Small jig or worm along canal edges and docks.

flbass.doing: Bass stage on offshore hydrilla edges and in deep holes in the hydrilla. The first fish move onto beds late in December on warm spells.
how: Lipless crankbait, speed worm or vibrating jig.
Punch hyacinth, pennywort or hydrilla with a Texas-rigged creature bait.

specks.doing: Schools leave the open water for pad fields, bulrush and Kissimmee grass that sit next to deeper water. A cold front pushes them back out.
how: Troll or drift minnow-tipped jigs along the outside of the pads and reeds.
Minnow under a cork in openings at the grass edge.
Fish the closest open water off the same grass.

bream.doing: Shellcracker move onto firm sand and shell near the grass ahead of the spring full moons; bluegill feed around reeds and docks.
how: Red wigglers on the bottom with a split shot.
Crickets or grass shrimp under a small float along reeds.

flbass.doing: Bass spawn on protected flats with scattered pads and grass clumps, while big fish also hold on offshore hydrilla clumps in 5 to 8 ft and shell bars with scattered grass in 4 to 5 ft. A winter tour event here was won on a lipless bait, a wacky worm and a swim jig.
how: 3/4 oz lipless crankbait, speed worm or vibrating jig over hydrilla clumps in 5 to 8 ft.
Lipless crankbait or Texas-rigged trick worm on shell with scattered grass.
Punch hydrilla, hyacinth and pennywort with 1 to 1.5 oz tungsten, especially near current like Goblets Cove.
Wacky Senko or creature bait on calm, clear, sunny days.

specks.doing: Specks hold near Shingle Creek mouth, Little Grassy Island and Goblets Cove, moving into the pads and reeds around the full moon.
how: Live minnows across open water near those spots.
Minnow under a cork along the reeds on the moon.

bream.doing: Shellcracker bed on the March and April full moons on firm sand and shell near grass. Bluegill start as the water warms.
how: Red wigglers on the bottom; work the area until you find the colony.
Small beetle spin along the edge of the flat.

flbass.doing: Post-spawn bass recover on grass lines and deeper hydrilla edges. Points that change from one kind of grass to another, like Brown's Point on the west side, stack fish.
how: Vibrating jig, swim jig or swimbait.
Walking bait or frog over pads near shell bars.

specks.doing: After the spawn, specks scatter to deeper grass edges, docks, bridges and channel edges. The bite slows as the water warms.
how: Minnows at dock pilings, bridges and fish attractors.
Small jig swum along the deep edge of the vegetation.

bream.doing: Bluegill bed in colonies on sand around each full moon from April on: the best bream fishing of the year, with fish near a pound on good lakes.
how: Under a cork over the beds or along reed lines.
In deep spatterdock and grass patches.
Popping bug or small spider at dawn and dusk.

flbass.doing: Bass hold on hydrilla lines at 8 to 10 ft or under the mats. Fish school early along main-lake hydrilla edges, current through the south-end lock concentrates them, and after rain they gather at moving water.
how: Topwater or lipless crankbait on schooling fish.
Shingle Creek, Partin Canal and the St. Cloud Canal.

specks.doing: The slowest season. Specks suspend in the deepest water, on fish attractors and in shade; fish early, late or at night.
how: Lights and minnows at bridges and deep docks.
Vertical jig or minnow at the depth you mark.

bream.doing: Bluegill keep spawning on each full moon; between moons they hold in deeper pads, grass patches and around docks. Fish early.
how: Grass shrimp in deep pads and hydrilla patches; anchor and chum lightly.
Worms and crickets along the walkways.

flbass.doing: Shad move into the creeks and shoreline grass, and bass follow them into open pockets.
how: Vibrating jig or crankbait along grass edges at points.

specks.doing: The speck bite picks up as the weather cools. Shingle Creek mouth, Little Grassy Island and Goblets Cove are the named spots.
how: FWC fish attractors are mapped online.

bream.doing: Bream feed hard in the grass as the water cools. Fewer beds, steady numbers.
how: Anchor near a thick hydrilla patch and fish grass shrimp or worms near the bottom.
Crickets under a cork along reed lines.

zones.name: Goblets Cove
zones.t: Protected spawning water where the St. Cloud Canal comes in; mats near current.

zones.name: West-side shell bars and flats
zones.t: Hydrilla flats, peppergrass lines and shell; Brown's Point is a transition point here.

zones.name: Shingle Creek mouth
zones.t: Moving water after rain; bass and specks.

zones.name: South-end lock
zones.t: Current through the lock to Cypress Lake.

zones.name: Friars Cove
zones.t: A protected cove on the southeast shore.

zones.name: Deepest open water
zones.t: Suspended specks; early, late or at night.

zones.name: Sand flats near reeds
zones.t: Shellcracker, then bluegill bed colonies around the islands.
